native_result.query: In which century did summed social capital peak, what individual social capital components like gold, monument etc increase?
native_result.HypoA: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?
native_result.HypoB: Summed social capital (Copper&Gold ZCU_AU + Amber Zamber + Monument Count ZMonument) peaked in the 14th-13th centuries BCE, exact maximum at BCE 1400 and 1300 (sum = 4.24 Z-units). At this peak the increasing components are Copper & Gold (record-high zone, +2.54) and Monument Count (+1.71, above baseline and rising +0.36 vs previous century); Amber is not elevated at the peak (-0.01, far below its BCE ~3000-3300 maximum). Independent interpolated-1yr cross-check and all-12 sensitivity sum both confirm the same 14th-century-BCE window.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Parse capital.csv (comma decimals) -> 39 century rows BCE 4300-500. 2) Verify each component is Z-standardized (mean~0, std~1) to justify equal weighting. 3) Primary index: per-century sum of ZCU_AU+Zamber+ZMonument -> peak BCE 1400/1300 (4.238), 2nd place BCE 1100/1200 (3.622), distinct 3rd BCE 2700 (2.959). 4) Component assessment at peak: value vs own long-run mean and local change vs preceding century (above-baseline and/or positive-change flags). 5) Cross-check on time_series_data.csv interpolated columns (century means, 100yr/c): top = 14th c. BCE (4.24). 6) Sensitivity: all-12 sum peaks BCE 1400 (14th c. BCE); 3-mean peaks BCE 1300. 7) Synthesized data-grounded hypothesis. Script: analysis_social_capital.py; outputs: social_capital_series.csv, analysis_summary.txt.

sub_hypo.text: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monument Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneously while summer social capital peaks.
sub_hypo.relations: Monument Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneously while summer social capital peaks; no column is explicitly identified for summer social capital.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?

sub_hypo.text: Summed social capital peaked at BCE 1400 and 1300, reaching 4.238 Z-units (rounded to 4.24), followed by BCE 1100/1200 at 3.622 and BCE 2700 at 2.959.
sub_hypo.context: Archaeological capital data covering 39 century rows from BCE 4300 to 500; components are Z-standardized with mean approximately zero and standard deviation approximately one.
sub_hypo.relations: The equally weighted sum ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument has its maximum at BCE 1400 and 1300, its second-highest value at BCE 1100/1200, and its distinct third-highest value at BCE 2700.

sub_hypo.text: At the social-capital peak, Copper & Gold was in its record-high zone at +2.54 Z-units, and Monument Count was above baseline at +1.71 and rising by +0.36 relative to the preceding century; Amber was not elevated at -0.01, far below its maximum around BCE 3000–3300.
sub_hypo.context: Component assessment at the BCE 1400/1300 social-capital peak, relative to each component's long-run mean and the preceding century.
sub_hypo.relations: Copper & Gold and Monument Count contribute positively to the summed peak; Monument Count also increases versus the preceding century. Amber is slightly below its baseline and below its earlier maximum.

sub_hypo.text: An independent cross-check using annually interpolated social-capital components and 100-year century means confirms a maximum of 4.24 in the 14th century BCE.
sub_hypo.context: Interpolated archaeological time-series data aggregated into century means using 100 years per century.
sub_hypo.relations: The sum of the three interpolated components, evaluated as century means, peaks in the same 14th-century-BCE window as the primary social-capital index.

sub_hypo.text: Sensitivity analysis using the sum of all 12 capital indicators peaks at BCE 1400, confirming the 14th-century-BCE window; the three-component mean peaks at BCE 1300.
sub_hypo.context: Sensitivity analysis of the archaeological capital data covering BCE 4300–500.
sub_hypo.relations: The all-12-indicator sum reaches its maximum at BCE 1400, while the mean of ZCU_AU, Zamber, and ZMonument reaches its maximum at BCE 1300.

At this peak the increasing components are Copper & Gold (record-high zone, +2.54) and Monument Count (+1.71, above baseline and rising +0.36 vs previous century); Amber is not elevated at the peak (-0.01, far below its BCE ~3000-3300 maximum). Independent interpolated-1yr cross-check and all-12 sensitivity sum both confirm the same 14th-century-BCE window.
